lawyer:
Md Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate — For Condemned Prisoner. 
Nikhilesh Dutta, Deputy Attorney-General and Layekuzzaman, Assistant Attorney-General — For the State.
parties:
State ------ Petitioner
VS.
Azharul  ------ Condemned Prisoner
full_judgment:
15. Mr Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the condemned prisoner submits that in the instant case the charge has not been properly framed as contemplated by sections 221/223/224 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and, as such, the trial against the accused persons have been vitiated due to non-compliance of the provisions of the said sections. The learned Advocate further submits that in the charge-sheet 14 persons have been cited as witnesses but out of them Sultan Mahmud, Shahanara, Amajan, Shahjahan have not been examined by the prosecution nor they have been tendered by the prosecution for cross-examination by the defence and there is also no explanation from the side of the prosecution as to why they could not examine these witnesses. Thus it is a case wherein the trial Court ought to have drawn an adverse presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act against the prosecution in that, if those witnesses were produced and examined before the trial Court they would not have supported the prosecution story. The learned Advocate further submits that on a close scrutiny of the PWs. it appears that there are a lot of discrepancies and contradictions but the learned trial Court in convicting and sentencing the condemned prisoner totally failed to consider that aspect of the case which has caused a miscarriage of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that in convicting the accused appellants the learned trial Court failed to properly sift the evidence adduced by the prosecution. The learned Advocate further submits that in the inquest report there are 14 witnesses out of whom the prosecution only examined three persons at the trial and, as such, this aspect of the case also ought to have been taken into consideration in disposing of the case by the trial Court. The learned Advocate further submits that in the instant case the evidence of the prosecution witnesses are dubious and tainted and, as such,they ought to have been properly and cautiously weighed by the trial Court in evaluating the evidentiary value of the depositions. The learned Advocate most emphatically submits that in the instant case the condemned prisoner and the other appellants are entitled to acquittal because the evidence of PWs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7 who claimed to be the eye-witness of the occurrence contradict the expert evidence of doctor PW 8 as to the nature and place of injury inflicted by the condemned prisoner Azharul on the body of deceased Momdel Hossain and, as such, it is a fit case where the accused appellants are entitled to get at least the benefit of doubt as the prosecution has failed to prove the manner of occurrence conclusively and to the satisfaction of the Court by cogent and sufficient evidence. The learned Advocate further submits that in the instant case the prosecution failed to examine the neighbouring witnesses and, as such, this casts doubt as to the genuineness of the prosecution case. The learned Advocate further submits that the local witnesses namely, PWs 1-7 are inter-related with each other and not a single disinterested and impartial witness has been examined in the instant case in support of the prosecution case which casts a heavy cloud over the prosecution case. The learned Advocate further submits that in the instant case there are vital omissions both in the First Information Report and in the depositions of alleged eye-witnesses and, as such, the accused appellants are entitled to get the benefit of doubt as the prosecution has failed to prove their case by cogent evidence. The learned Advocate finally submits alternatively that if his submissions made on merit are rejected by this Court then also the condemned prisoner''s sentence is liable to be committed to imprisonment for life because the judgment was delivered on 29-11-92 and since then he is passing his days in the condemned cell in the mental agony, frustration and sufferings and for this he relies on the decision reported in 49 DLR 381. 

 23. There is another aspect of the case that is, that in the instant case 14 persons have been cited as witnesses in the charge sheet but out of them 4 persons have not been examined by the prosecution and there is no explanation why they could not produce and examine them before the trial Court and, as such, an adverse presumption can easily be drawn against the prosecution for withholding these charge sheet witnesses. In this connection it may also be mentioned that although PW 2 claims to be an eye-witness of the occurrence yet her name was not mentioned in the First Information Report.
